To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
unilateral lesions of the frontal lobes in the early post-acute phase of a stroke lead to a bias of response-selection in favour of the ipsilateral hemisphere.
unilateral lesions in the early stages of development of the brain result in the implementation of opposite response-biases, in each hemisphere of that brain, for the same stimulus.
the left hemisphere (LH) and the right hemisphere (RH) are differentially involved in the implementation of opposed response biases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the left hemisphere is dominant in implementing the response-biases that are required to solve a problem in a particular way.
the question whether the brain can learn to perform an action in a specific manner, or whether it is constrained by the structure of its motor apparatus.
the development of the brain's ability to process and respond to the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the left brain hemisphere is responsible for the generation of positive response-biases, while the right brain hemisphere is responsible, at least in part, for the generation of negative response-biases.

, the left hemisphere is responsible for the implementation of positive response-biases (i.e., positive response-bias in the form of the implementation of a positive response-bias) and that the right hemisphere is responsible for implementation of negative response-biases, i.e., negative response-bias in form of the implementation a negative response-bias.
the left hemisphere is dominant in processing the verbal material, whereas the right hemisphere is dominant in the nonverbal processing of material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain is not a single entity but rather is a collection of separate systems, each with its own function.
the brain’s left hemisphere is biased to respond to the world with an optimistic, positive bias, and its right hemisphere with a pessimistic, negative bias.
the left hemisphere is biased to respond to the left and that the correct hemisphere is biased to reply to the right, but that these biases can be reversed by unilateral brain lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain is not a single entity.
the right hemisphere of the brain is responsible for the implementation of response-biases that are opposite to the response-bias of the left hemisphere.
the brain has a strong preference for the opposite response-bias.
